title: Outcome
description: What running a task's lines produced.

ok.description: Whether every line ran and found everything in order.

runs.description:
Each line that ran, in order: up to the first that failed, for a task
whose lines lean on each other ([`Task::chained`]).

Run.description:
What one command line produced, as a terminal would show it, with the
code of everything that went wrong beside its words.

command.description: The line, as it would be typed into a shell ([`shell`]).

error.description: Why it could not run, when it could not.

ok.description:
Whether it ran and found everything in order: what its exit status
would have said.

stderr.description:
Each line it said on stderr, with its code; none for a hint or a
note, which no code is given to.

Said.description:
An error as a serialized type holds one: its code, for a front end to act
on, and its message, for whoever reads it.

Built where the type is serialized, or kept in what a front end reads
(the workspace's snapshot), in place of the error, since an error
holds what JSON has no shape for (an `io::Error`, a parser's own), and
only these two are meant to leave core. Its fields are public for a
front end that reads the snapshot as Rust rather than as JSON, the TUI.

message.description:
Written through [`redacted`](crate::url::redacted), as every URL
is: an error can quote one, a source's among them, and what built
the error is no promise that it carries no credential.

Warning.description:
One line a command says beside what it reports, on stderr: a warning, a
note, a hint, or an error about one part of what it did; and the code of
what it says, when what it says has one.

The text is what a terminal shows, word for word, `warning: ` and all.
The code rides beside it for the panel, which acts on a condition by its
code rather than by matching English that is reworded whenever it is
made clearer: the code core gives what went wrong ([`mindflayer_core::code`]),
or the CLI's own ([`CliError::code`]). A line with none says something no
code is given to: a hint, a note, or what the CLI makes of what it found
rather than something that went wrong. Kept beside the text rather than
in a list of its own beside the lines, which every line pushed would have
to keep in step with.

Serialized as it is, `{"text": ..., "code": ...}`, in what a run of the
panel's backend says (`backend::Run`): the line a terminal shows, and
the code beside it.
